title: The Joke That Made Everyone Laugh

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older and another villager)

collection.description: A villager is proudest of a joke that once made everyone laugh: tell the joke, or explain why it matters.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) asks (subject) what (subject.he/she) is proudest of in (subject.his/her) whole life. (subject) thinks about it seriously. Not (subject.his/her) work. Not the hut (subject.he/she) built. Not the famous fish. "Once," (subject.he/she) says, "at a feast, years ago, I made a joke, and EVERYONE laughed. All of them. Even the grumpy ones. Even the babies."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) wants to hear it. (subject) tells it. It's about a pig and a coconut. (friend) doesn't laugh. (subject) explains that you had to be there, and the pig was also there, and that's what made it. (friend) still doesn't laugh. (subject) doesn't mind in the least. (subject.He/she) tells it again later, to (subject.him/her)self, and laughs until (subject.he/she) cries.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Why that?" asks (friend). (subject) thinks. "Because for a moment, everybody was happy at the same time, and I did that. You can't plan it. It just happened, and I was the one who made it happen." (friend) thinks about this. It's a better answer than (friend.he/she) expected. (friend.He/she) decides to try making everyone laugh at the next feast. (friend.He/she) doesn't. But (friend.he/she) tries.
